questions.question: An encroachment happens when:

options.text: A driver misses their scheduled basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one part of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the basic skills test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look means:

options.text: A driver checks the dashboard gauges.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver leaves the vehicle and walks to the back to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver leaves the vehicle and walks to the back to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look is when you leave your seat, open the door, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check where it is. For straight-line backing, you can only do one look. For other exercises, you can do up to two looks.

questions.question: School bus doors must stay closed while driving, except when:

options.text: Crossing railroad tracks.
You need to cool down the bus.
There is no car next to the bus.

questions.explanation: School bus doors must stay closed while the bus is moving. The only exception is when crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: After students get off at school, the driver should:

options.text: Not worry about where the students go.
Leave once students have entered the building.
Walk through the bus to check for sleeping students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for sleeping students.
questions.explanation: After students leave, walk through the entire bus to check for sleeping students, hidden students, and items left behind. Make sure students leave in an orderly way while you watch them.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, students:

options.text: Must get off the bus.
Should stay on the bus but move to an area away from the fire.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.explanation: If there is a fire or a threat of fire on a school bus, you must evacuate all students right away.

questions.question: If a tornado is near and there is no shelter, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby ditch
To the closest tree
Near a river

questions.explanation: If you must evacuate students from a bus in the path of a tornado, take them to a shelter in a nearby building first. If no building is available, take them to a ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that could flood and stay far enough away so the bus cannot fall on them.

questions.question: School bus mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: While you are driving.
Before you start driving.
By the students.

questions.explanation: Always check that all mirrors are adjusted correctly before you begin driving the school bus.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, exiting your vehicle incorrectly will result in:

options.text: Failure of only that exercise.
An extra point taken off your final score.
Automatic failure of the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When you exit your vehicle during the test, you must face the vehicle and hold on with three points of contact at all times. If it is a bus, you must use the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will automatically fail the entire test.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check the power steering fluid level.
Make sure the power steering fluid is above the full mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will show where the power steering fluid is located. You will check that the fluid is at a safe level. It should not go above the full mark.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you receive points against your score if you:

options.text: Pull forward once.
Check your positioning.
Cross over exercise boundary lines.

questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each touch or cross is an error and counts against your score.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be hazardous for passengers.
Should be supervised by someone other than the driver.
Should be done when refueling.

questions.explanation: Passengers may trip when getting on or off the bus. The driver should remind passengers to watch their step when exiting.

questions.question: An inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: Monitor passengers.
Inspect the outside of the bus.
See vehicles trying to switch lanes.

questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror watches student activity inside the bus. Adjust it to see every student, including those directly behind the driver.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the right side of a bus.
On the steering wheel of a bus.
Above the windshield inside a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside a bus.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use this mirror to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: During the drive.
Before beginning to drive.
After the drive is completed.

questions.explanation: It is important to adjust mirrors properly before operating a school bus. Always check each mirror before you start driving.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: See passengers.
See potential hazards on the road.
See vehicles trying to switch lanes.

questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror in a school bus watches student activity inside the bus.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Hop directly from their seat to the ground.
Maintain at least one point of contact with their vehicle.
Be turned to face their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned to face their vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during a driving test, face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the bus driver should:

options.text: Not use their mirrors.
Approach the stop with caution.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.explanation: A school bus driver should always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: If taking the driving test and the route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take the test again on a route that does include a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Can be hazardous for passengers.
Does not need to be supervised.
Should be done while refueling.

questions.explanation: More students are killed during loading and unloading of school buses than while riding in them. School bus drivers must follow proper safety procedures during these times.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
Be seated as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the back row only after all other seats are filled.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Students are safer closer to the front of the bus, especially in a rear-end crash. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.
